title: Is Washington Finally Ready to Take On Big Tech?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想一下，早在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里，我作为DJ，每晚都要带上300张你最珍爱的宝贝去上班，你把一个DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Katrin Benholt.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》的我，是卡特琳·本霍尔特。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This week, in a San Francisco courtroom, federal regulators are fighting to block one of the biggest deals in the history of Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 本周，在旧金山的一家法庭上，联邦监管机构正在全力阻止硅谷历史上最大规模的交易之一。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague David McCabe on the architect of that lawsuit, Lina Khan, and the growing campaign by the Biden administration to finally rein in big tech.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·麦凯布将为我们讲述该诉讼的幕后推手莉娜·汗，以及拜登政府为最终遏制大型科技公司而不断壮大的行动。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月29日，星期四。

sentences.en: David, this is only the second episode I've hosted of The Daily, and I think it is the first the show has ever devoted to the Federal Trade Commission.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这只是我主持的第二期《每日新闻》，我想这也是节目有史以来第一次专门报道联邦贸易委员会。

sentences.en: And that may be because, frankly, even saying those words just made me a little sleepy.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为，坦白说，仅仅说出这几个字就让我有点犯困。

sentences.en: Tell me why I shouldn't be sleepy.
sentences.zh: 告诉我为什么我不该犯困。

sentences.en: You shouldn't be sleepy because the Federal Trade Commission is the regulator that is tasked with making sure that capitalism works in the United States.
sentences.zh: 你不该犯困，因为联邦贸易委员会是负责确保美国资本主义正常运转的监管机构。

sentences.en: So the cases that they bring are bellwethers for how big companies end up getting regulated and how powerful they are able to become.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们提起诉讼的案件，成为了大公司最终如何被监管以及它们能变得多强大的风向标。

sentences.en: And one of those cases is playing out this week.
sentences.zh: 其中一个案件就在本周上演。

sentences.en: That makes a lot of sense, and that has woken me up.
sentences.zh: 这很有道理，这让我清醒过来了。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about this case.
sentences.zh: 好的，跟我讲讲这个案子吧。

sentences.en: We're going to start with one of the biggest deals of the decade,
sentences.zh: 我们要从这十年中最大的一笔交易开始说起，

sentences.en: Microsoft's long-running $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard.
sentences.zh: 微软长期推进的耗资690亿美元收购动视暴雪案。

sentences.en: So the Federal Trade Commission is trying to stop Microsoft, which makes the Xbox video game console, along with being involved in a ton of other businesses,
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会正试图阻止微软——该公司制造Xbox电子游戏机，同时还涉足大量其他业务——

sentences.en: from buying Activision Blizzard, which publishes some of the biggest video games in the world.
sentences.zh: 收购动视暴雪，该公司发行了世界上一些最大型的电子游戏。

sentences.en: Including Activision's first-person shooter, Call of Duty.
sentences.zh: 包括动视的第一人称射击游戏《使命召唤》。

sentences.en: Probably most importantly, the Call of Duty franchise.
sentences.zh: 可能最重要的是，《使命召唤》系列。

sentences.en: And one of the most popular mobile games, Candy Crush.
sentences.zh: 还有最受欢迎的手游之一《糖果粉碎传奇》。

sentences.en: And right now in San Francisco, a judge is deciding whether or not the FTC's case is good enough that they should temporarily block this deal from closing
sentences.zh: 目前在旧金山，一位法官正在裁决联邦贸易委员会的案子是否足够充分，以至于他们应该暂时阻止这笔交易的完成，

sentences.en: so that this big challenge to this acquisition can go forward.
sentences.zh: 从而让这场对该收购案的重大挑战得以推进。

sentences.en: After all, while it was pitched as an acquisition, in some ways it's more of a merger between two of the five biggest gaming companies globally.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，虽然它被宣传为一次收购，但在某些方面，它更像是全球五大游戏公司中两家之间的合并。

sentences.en: And this case is actually important in a bigger way, which is that it's a key indicator for whether or not government agencies like the Federal Trade Commission
sentences.zh: 这个案子实际上在更深远的意义上也很重要，那就是它是政府机构（如联邦贸易委员会）

sentences.en: can stop big tech from getting bigger.
sentences.zh: 能否阻止大型科技公司变得更大的一个关键指标。

sentences.en: So explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: How do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: So over the last five or so years, there's been really mounting concern, not just in Washington, but in world capitals like Brussels and London,
sentences.zh: 所以在过去的五年左右时间里，人们的担忧与日俱增，不仅是在华盛顿，在布鲁塞尔和伦敦等世界首都也是如此，

sentences.en: over how big Silicon Valley companies have gotten.
sentences.zh: 担忧硅谷的大公司已经变得多么庞大。

sentences.en: And we're talking really here about five companies.
sentences.zh: 我们这里所指的实际上是五家公司。

sentences.en: Amazon, Google, Apple, Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, and Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊、谷歌、苹果、拥有Facebook和Instagram的Meta，以及微软。

sentences.en: And the critics of these companies believe that they've become these kind of insurmountable gatekeepers for commerce and communications and basically like our whole lives online.
sentences.zh: 这些公司的批评者认为，它们已经成为商业、通信以及我们基本上所有在线生活的某种不可逾越的守门人。

sentences.en: And governments have responded by saying there's a problem here.
sentences.zh: 政府的回应是指出这里存在问题。

sentences.en: But now the question is, can anybody actually take action to rein these companies in, or will they just get more powerful?
sentences.zh: 但现在的问题是，是否真的有人能采取行动来遏制这些公司，还是它们只会变得更加强大？

sentences.en: And it seems to be one of those rare issues where you actually have support on both sides of the aisle, where you kind of have mainstream figures, you know, from Bernie Sanders
sentences.zh: 这似乎是少数几个能同时获得两党支持的罕见议题之一，在这里，你从主流政治人物身上——你知道的，从伯尼·桑德斯

sentences.en: to Joe Biden and Josh Hawley, all of whom sort of agree something needs to be done to regulate big tech.
sentences.zh: 到乔·拜登和乔什·霍利——都能看到他们都某种程度上认为需要采取措施来监管大型科技公司。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the rare bipartisan consensus in Washington right now that these companies have gotten really big and really powerful and the government maybe should do something about it.
sentences.zh: 这是华盛顿目前罕见的两党共识，即这些公司已经变得非常巨大且非常强大，政府也许应该对此做点什么。

sentences.en: But Congress in particular has really struggled to figure out what that is.
sentences.zh: 但国会尤其在弄清楚该怎么做方面遇到了很大困难。

sentences.en: They proposed a lot of laws and they haven't gone anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了很多法律，但都无疾而终。

sentences.en: And so when Congress can't make new laws to regulate the tech giants, it means the only tool that the government has to pursue these companies is the laws on the books.
sentences.zh: 因此，当国会无法制定新法律来监管科技巨头时，这就意味着政府用来对付这些公司的唯一工具就是现有的法律。

sentences.en: And that means that the questions about are these companies too powerful and what should the government do have really fallen to regulators like the Federal Trade Commission.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，关于这些公司是否过于强大以及政府应该做些什么的问题，实际上已经落在了像联邦贸易委员会这样的监管机构肩上。

sentences.en: And that agency has started to take on these tech giants in a way that it hasn't before.
sentences.zh: 该机构开始以一种前所未有的方式向这些科技巨头宣战。

sentences.en: And the architect and face of that pivot is the FTC's new chair, Lina Khan.
sentences.zh: 而这一转型背后的设计师和面孔，就是联邦贸易委员会的新任主席莉娜·汗。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about Lina Khan.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么跟我讲讲莉娜·汗吧。

sentences.en: So Lina Khan has had a meteoric rise to lead the Federal Trade Commission.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗可以说是以火箭般的速度崛起并执掌联邦贸易委员会的。

sentences.en: And it all really starts in 2017.
sentences.zh: 这一切其实都始于2017年。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm Lina Khan.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是莉娜·汗。

sentences.en: I'm a visiting fellow at Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 我是耶鲁法学院的访问学者。

sentences.en: So in 2017, not that long ago,
sentences.zh: 所以在2017年，也就是不久前，

sentences.en: Lina Khan was a law student and she was at Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗还是一名法学院学生，当时她在耶鲁法学院。

sentences.en: I wrote a piece called
sentences.zh: 我写了一篇名为

sentences.en: Amazon's Antitrust Paradox that tells the story of Amazon's rise.
sentences.zh: 《亚马逊的反垄断悖论》的文章，讲述了亚马逊崛起的故事。

sentences.en: And she writes this essay for the Law Review, as a lot of law students do, right?
sentences.zh: 正如许多法学院学生所做的那样，她为《法律评论》撰写了这篇关于亚马逊的文章，对吧？

sentences.en: About Amazon.
sentences.zh: 关于亚马逊。

sentences.en: I think increasingly businesses are not able to compete on the merits with Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我认为越来越多的企业无法在实力上与亚马逊公平竞争。

sentences.en: And I actually think the way that she describes it in the paper is really instructive of how she views the company in these tech platforMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为她在论文中描述这一现象的方式，对于她如何看待这家公司和这些科技平台具有很好的启发意义。

sentences.en: So she writes, in addition to being a retailer,
sentences.zh: 因此她写道，除了是一家零售商之外，

sentences.en: Amazon is now a marketing platform, a delivery and logistics network, a payment service, a credit lender, an auction house, a major book publisher,
sentences.zh: 亚马逊现在还是一个营销平台、一个配送和物流网络、一个支付服务商、一个信贷出借方、一个拍卖行、一家大型图书出版商、

sentences.en: a producer of television and films, a fashion designer, a hardware manufacturer, and a leading host of cloud server space.
sentences.zh: 一家电视和电影制片商、一个时装设计师、一个硬件制造商，以及云服务器空间的主要托管商。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, we all know how huge Amazon is in our lives, but it's quite startling to hear this list of things that it does.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都知道亚马逊在我们的生活中有多么庞大，但听到它所做的这些事情的清单，还是相当令人震惊的。

sentences.en: You know, one company that spans so many industries and roles basically sells things, competes against others selling things, and owns the platform where all of these transactions
sentences.zh: 你知道，一家跨越如此多行业和角色的公司，基本上既在销售商品，又与其他人销售的商品竞争，还拥有这一切交易发生的平台

sentences.en: happen as well.
sentences.zh: 本身。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this idea of a platform business is really crucial to understanding
sentences.zh: 而这种平台型企业的概念，对于理解

sentences.en: Lena Kahn's concerns.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗的关切至关重要。

sentences.en: Because it's not just Amazon.
sentences.zh: 因为这不仅仅是关于亚马逊。

sentences.en: Amazon is a clear example of it.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊是一个明显的例子。

sentences.en: But Apple runs a platform in the form of its app store, right?
sentences.zh: 但苹果通过其应用商店运营着一个平台，对吧？

sentences.en: Apple sells apps.
sentences.zh: 苹果销售应用程序。

sentences.en: They also run the main store where other people sell apps.
sentences.zh: 他们还运营着一个主要商店，别人可以在那里销售应用程序。

sentences.en: Google runs a search engine that includes results from websites like, say, reviews of a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 谷歌运营着一个搜索引擎，其中包含来自各个网站的结果，比如餐馆评论。

sentences.en: Google also has its own review service.
sentences.zh: 谷歌也有自己的评论服务。

sentences.en: So what she's articulating is that these sort of mega platforms have grown without a lot of attention from government and are posing real problems for competition in the economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，她所阐明的是，这些超级平台在没有受到政府太多关注的情况下不断壮大，并对经济中的竞争构成了真正的挑战。

sentences.en: So David, what is the solution she proposes in this paper?
sentences.zh: 那么大卫，她在论文中提出的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: So this is where we go back to the past a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们稍微回顾一下过去的时候了。

sentences.en: Lena Kahn is telling a story about history.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗是在讲述一个关于历史的故事。

sentences.en: Antitrust laws were passed around the turn of the century at a time when there were these big trusts, the most classic, which is Standard Oil,
sentences.zh: 反垄断法是在世纪之交通过的，当时存在着这些大型托拉斯，最典型的就是标准石油公司，

sentences.en: which made the Rockefeller family rich.
sentences.zh: 它让洛克菲勒家族变得富有。

sentences.en: And over time, they were used to break up Standard Oil, to break up other big companies.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它们被用来拆分标准石油公司，拆分其他大公司。

sentences.en: But the reality is that some of antitrust law is written down in the laws.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，反垄断法一部分是明文写在法律里的。

sentences.en: And some of antitrust law is about how judges interpret it.
sentences.zh: 而另一部分反垄断法则在于法官如何对其进行解释。

sentences.en: And what Lena Kahn is saying is that in the 1970s, conservative lawyers, academics, economists were able to shift the way antitrust law is understood by the courts.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗所说的是，在20世纪70年代，保守派律师、学者和经济学家成功地改变了法院对反垄断法的理解方式。

sentences.en: And that instead of considering a whole range of harms to competition, to the economy, that the courts were now basically considering, in most cases, one factor to decide
sentences.zh: 他们不再考虑对竞争、对经济的广泛损害，而是让法院在大多数情况下基本上只考虑一个因素来决定

sentences.en: whether or not something violated antitrust law.
sentences.zh: 某事是否违反了反垄断法。

sentences.en: And that was whether or not it hurt consumers, and particularly whether or not it hurt consumers in the form of higher prices.
sentences.zh: 那个因素就是它是否损害了消费者，尤其是它是否以更高价格的形式损害了消费者。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that since the 1970s, the definition of antitrust in a way was that as long as prices remained low and consumers happy, regulators left
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，自20世纪70年代以来，反垄断的定义在某种程度上变成了：只要价格保持低位且消费者高兴，监管机构就对

sentences.en: big companies alone.
sentences.zh: 大公司置之不理。

sentences.en: Yeah, for the most part.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: And so in this paper,
sentences.zh: 因此在这篇论文中，

sentences.en: Lena Kahn is basically saying that the government and the courts should widen the scope of what falls under antitrust laws in a way that she would argue basically returns it
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗基本上是在说，政府和法院应该扩大属于反垄断法管辖范围的事项，用她的话来说，这基本上是将它恢复为

sentences.en: to the tool it once was in American history.
sentences.zh: 美国历史上曾经发挥过作用的工具。

sentences.en: That even though Amazon keeps prices very low, that it's still engaging in all these practices that could harm competition, potentially to the detriment of people,
sentences.zh: 即使亚马逊保持着非常低的价格，它仍然在从事所有这些可能损害竞争的做法，并可能损害人们的利益，

sentences.en: including other smaller companies, who sell on its platform.
sentences.zh: 包括在其平台上销售的其他较小公司的利益。

sentences.en: So price alone is no longer like a useful and valuable indicator for when to apply antitrust practices.
sentences.zh: 因此，价格单独来看不再是一个有用且有价值的指标，用来判断何时应适用反垄断法。

sentences.en: That's exactly what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 这正是你所说的。

sentences.en: So, David, one way to think about this as I'm listening to you is that even though antitrust laws were originally designed to prevent the concentration of corporate power,
sentences.zh: 那么大卫，当我听你讲述时，有一个想法是，尽管反垄断法最初旨在防止企业权力的集中，

sentences.en: ironically, it seems that in recent decades, it's almost like they have favored market concentration by focusing so much on lower prices and consumer happiness.
sentences.zh: 但具有讽刺意味的是，在近几十年来，由于过于关注较低的价格和消费者的幸福感，它似乎几乎在偏袒市场集中。

sentences.en: And now,
sentences.zh: 而现在，

sentences.en: Lena Kahn wants the FTC to return to that original mission.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗希望联邦贸易委员会回归最初的使命。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's how she sees the central failing of the government in the preceding, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就是她如何看待政府在之前，你知道的，

sentences.en: 30 years.
sentences.zh: 30年里的核心失误。

sentences.en: That they essentially were asleep at the switch while these companies got extremely big and extremely powerful.
sentences.zh: 那就是当这些公司变得极其庞大和极其强大时，他们基本上是在玩忽职守。

sentences.en: And ultimately, I think the case that Lena Kahn is making is that, yes, consumers are one part of the broader world, but the government needs to think about the economy
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我认为莉娜·汗提出的论点是，是的，消费者是更广泛世界的一部分，但政府需要更广泛地看待经济，

sentences.en: more broadly than it needs to think about.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅局限于某一方面。

sentences.en: Does concentration in the economy mean workers get paid less?
sentences.zh: 经济中的集中是否意味着工人的薪水变低了？

sentences.en: Does it mean that it's harder to start a startup that might come up with some sort of genius, innovative product?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着更难建立一家能够想出某种天才创新产品的初创公司？

sentences.en: And that when you consider all of those things together, that you have a healthier and more dynamic economy and ultimately democracy.
sentences.zh: 当你把所有这些因素综合起来考虑时，你就会拥有一个更健康、更有活力的经济，并最终拥有更健康的民主。

sentences.en: And how do people react to your paper?
sentences.zh: 人们对你的论文作何反应？

sentences.en: So with the caveat that we're talking about a law review article, it goes viral.
sentences.zh: 带着我们讨论的是一篇法学院学术期刊文章这一前提，它火了。

sentences.en: In a report for the Yale Law Journal,
sentences.zh: 在为《耶鲁法律杂志》撰写的一份报告中，

sentences.en: Lena Kahn writes that Amazon's dominance may soon challenge current antitrust laws.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗写道，亚马逊的统治地位可能很快会挑战现有的反垄断法。

sentences.en: She joins us now to explain why...
